8.2a — Boss Body, Health Bar & Phases

The spec exists (8.1a); today the boss gets a body, a number that says how alive it is, a BAR the player can watch fall, and the phase thresholds that make it change its mind. Health first, attacks later — a boss you cannot hurt cannot be tuned.

Build Lab ~30 min

Step 1 — the body. Big sprite, big collider, on the "Enemy" physics layer (your 7.2a layers pay off today: boss ignores boss, player passes decoration). If you have starter art, scale a mobile enemy up 3×; a placeholder rectangle is also fine and honest.

Step 2 — the health, in the StatManager's voice. The starter keeps player stats in a singleton; your boss is a scene-local boss, so it owns its own numbers — new script, same style:

public class BossManager : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private int maxHealth = 20;
    [SerializeField] private int phaseTwoAt = 10;   // 50%
    [SerializeField] private int phaseThreeAt = 4;  // 20%
    public static BossManager boss;
    private int currentHealth;
    private int currentPhase = 1;

    private void Awake()
    {
        boss = this;
        currentHealth = maxHealth;
    }

    public void ChangeHealth(int amount)
    {
        currentHealth += amount;
        currentHealth = Mathf.Max(currentHealth, 0);

        if (currentHealth <= 0)
        {
            Die();
        }
        else if (currentHealth <= phaseThreeAt && currentPhase == 2)
        {
            EnterPhase(3);
        }
        else if (currentHealth <= phaseTwoAt && currentPhase == 1)
        {
            EnterPhase(2);
        }
    }

    private void EnterPhase(int phase)
    {
        currentPhase = phase;
        Debug.Log("PHASE " + phase);
        // 8.4a: each phase swaps attack cooldowns / movement
    }

    private void Die()
    {
        Debug.Log("BOSS DOWN");
        // 8.5a: door opens, win path
        Destroy(gameObject);
    }
}

Read the threshold logic out loud: phase changes only fire DOWNWARD (currentPhase == checks) — a heal in Phase 2 cannot re-trigger Phase 2's entrance. Why does the state guard matter here more than it did for the lever (5.2a)?

Step 3 — the bar. UI the honest way: a Slider (GameObject → UI → Slider) anchored top-center. In BossManager:

[SerializeField] private Slider healthBar;

private void Update()
{
    if (healthBar != null)
    {
        healthBar.maxValue = maxHealth;
        healthBar.value = currentHealth;
    }
}

Why a bar instead of a number: the bar shows the pace of victory — the last sliver is drama a number cannot reach.

Bug Hunt: Phase bugs

  1. Remove the currentPhase guards. Hit the boss from 12 → 9 in one big hit (phase 2 fires) — then a heal... no, simpler: hit 9 → 8 → 7. How many times did EnterPhase(2) run, and what did the boss's entrance animation do?
  2. Set phaseTwoAt ABOVE maxHealth (say 30 of 20). What happens on the FIRST hit — and why is "phase thresholds are less than maxHealth" a spec invariant (8.1a arithmetic again)?
  3. Health goes negative from a huge hit (Mathf.Max removed). Phase 3 fires, then Die fires... but wait, which else-if ran first — and why did the boss SKIP phase 3's entrance entirely? Is that a bug or a feature (argue)?
  4. Two BossManager instances in the scene (you cloned the boss). Which one does BossManager.boss point at — and why did the starter's StatManager fight for singleton status in 2.1a too?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Phase feel

  1. Give EnterPhase a VISIBLE effect today, even before attacks: flash the sprite color, shake the camera (a transform jitter for 0.3s), play a sound. Why must the player KNOW the phase changed within one second?
  2. Tune your spec's arithmetic against the real bar: poke the boss with the debug console (BossManager.boss.ChangeHealth(-1)) — how many pokes to phase 2? Does the bar's pace match your 8.1a prediction?
  3. Commit + push: "8.2a: boss body + phases + bar".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Build BossManager with guarded phase thresholds
  • Wire a UI slider to boss health and explain bar-vs-number
  • Explain why phase transitions fire once, downward only
  • Test phase logic by poking health from the console
